title: Red-green color deficiency prevalence and color-only coding risk
statement:
Population surveys show inherited red-green color deficiency affects about 8% of men and 0.4% of women of European descent and 4% to 6.5% of men of Chinese and Japanese ethnicity, so red versus green status coding and low-luminance hue pairs will be misread by a meaningful share of visitors and color must not carry meaning alone.

Options:
- Color plus icon plus word: Status colors always paired with an icon and a text label (for example a check mark and the word 'Success') (fits: clear, trustworthy, professional)
- Blue-orange state palette: Blue and orange (or blue and yellow) for two-state emphasis instead of red and green, still combined with labels (fits: modern, confident, calm)
- Luminance-differentiated pairs: Palette pairs that differ in lightness as well as hue, verified in a red-green color deficiency simulator before sign-off (fits: technical, careful, polished)
- Direct labels over hue: Pricing tiers, charts and legends identified by direct labels or patterns, not by hue alone (fits: data-driven, clear, analytical)
appliesWhen: Applies to: general web. Audience: general.
